northStar: A visitor can answer where to enter the beach today in under ten seconds without confusing official access, derived convenience, and ocean safety.

userDecisionUsefulness.description: Immediate activity/area-specific answer, directional access, hours, tide context and official handoff.

dataTruthAndSourceFidelity.description: NPS is the eligibility gate; source failure is conservative; tide/surf/transport boundaries are explicit.

mapAndGeographicComprehension.description: Real geographic map, verified-only coordinates, understandable legend and complete list fallback.

repeatVisitValue.description: Status-change comparison, source timestamps and next meaningful tide/access context.

searchValue.description: Distinct canonical intent, crawlable answer/context, query-aligned metadata and no ramp doorway pages.

mobileUsabilityAndPerformance.description: 390px-friendly first answer loads before map complexity and has responsive controls.

maintainability.description: Ramp registry, parser, decision helpers and source contracts are isolated and testable.

accessibility.description: Semantic controls, aria state, readable contrast, reduced-motion support and non-map fallback.

lossFunction.formula: falseAccessClaims*10 + staleOrUnlabeledOfficialData*8 + unsafeImplication*8 + wrongGeographicAssociation*7 + userCannotIdentifyBestRamp*6 + mapConfusion*5 + firstScreenJargon*4 + unnecessaryClicks*3 + latency*3 + seoDuplication*3 + visualClutter*2
lossFunction.principle: The largest avoidable failure is a confident false access claim. No numerical product score can override a hard veto.

hardVetoes: A known closed ramp can be recommended as best access.
Missing or unparseable NPS access becomes open or otherwise produces a positive ORV recommendation.
Tide is presented as proof of vehicle safety, sand firmness or driveability.
Directional access is collapsed in a way that changes official semantics.
Map coordinates are interpolated or fabricated.
Pedestrian-only access is represented as fully closed.
Rip-current risk is represented as official NPS ORV closure status.
High rip-current risk is hidden from beach-day users.
The canonical is wrong, noindex is present, the public path 404s, or the live API fails.
Precise location is required to use the product.
Thin indexable ramp pages are mass-produced at launch.

production: API HTTP 200 or explicit conservative 503 on NPS failure
